text:
maria: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-routing tweak we started seeing intermittent OOMs on M40 pools. small spike at ~21:03 UTC, p99 token latency up ~1.2% for short-chat workloads.

chen: any smoke trace or flame?

maria: pushing profile now, but initial heap snapshots show more tiny free slots (lots of 256B fragments) in the kv slab. looks like larger workspace allocations are failing and triggering emergency demote -> extra prefetch churn. link: https://internal-redwood/perf/trace/ae3b2f (private)

alex: hmm. could be interaction between the new kernel's workspace rounding and our slab packing. that kernel tends to allocate 3-4x the minimal workspace for some attention paths, leading to more slot breakup.

sasha: do we have numbers on fragmentation delta?

maria: yes — comparing baseline -> post-change on a 4h window: free-slot-count +28%, avg-frag-size down 18%, effective usable-cache down ~9% for 1k-8k sequence mix. also saw ~12 OOMs across 1200 hosts in the window (small but reproducible).

chen: thanks. can you paste the allocator config for that run?

maria: here — run config snippet:

```yaml
allocator:
  slab_size: 4096
  micro_slot_size: 256
  slot_pack_factor: 0.8   # current
  slot_reuse_window_ms: 15000
kv_cache:
  prefill_threshold_tokens: 128
  per_request_soft_cap: 128
  demote_policy: eager_on_prefill_failure
```

alex: two quick levers to try: 1) reduce micro_slot_size to 128 for this workload class (pack more tightly), 2) lower slot_pack_factor to 0.6 so the allocator prefers compacting slots before creating new ones. my sim run showed ~7% fewer fragments with those settings.

sasha: curious about prefill vs on-decode tradeoff here — demote/eager prefill seems to be causing extra allocations when prefill fails. Does switching prefill->on-decode reduce peak working set?

maria: short answer: yes for these traces. we instrumented two runs:
- prefill-first: average peak GPU mem 27.1GB, tail OOMs at high concurrency
- on-decode: average peak 24.9GB, decode-latency p50 ~+0.6% but p99 stable
so on-decode shifts cost to latency but reduces peak and fragmentation because we reuse smaller decode-time buffers.

chen: nice — can we make on-decode the fallback when slot fragmentation > X? i.e. dynamic policy: prefill when fragmentation < 12% else on-decode.

alex: yeah, implementable. maybe tie the threshold to slot_reuse_window too. if reuse window short, prefill less useful.

maria: proposal: add a soft_request_cap per-request that gates prefetch attempts. rough config:

```yaml
kv_runtime.policy.dynamic_prefetch:
  enabled: true
  fragment_threshold_pct: 12
  per_request_soft_cap_tokens: 64
  fallback_mode: on_decode
```

sasha: good. we should also add a lightweight offline simulator to estimate fragmentation impact before rollout. current simulator assumes uniform slot sizes which misses micro-slot packing effects.

chen: agree. i'll whip up a quick sim patch that replays allocator traces and reports frag% and effective cache capacity. can include a mode to emulate kernel workspace rounding.

infra-bot: Deploy queued for canary cluster "m40-pack-test" — CI checks passed.

maria: next steps:
- chen: sim + branch to toggle slot_pack_factor and micro_slot_size (priority)
- alex: run 2 canary configs: (a) micro_slot=128, pack=0.6 (b) keep micro_slot=256 but slot_pack=0.65 + per-request-soft-cap 64
- sasha: add perf regression guard for p99 token latency on short-chat workload

everyone: thumbs-up or :thumbsup: if you agree to that plan

alex: :+1:
chen: :thumbsup:
sasha: :thumbsup:
maria: thanks — i'll coordinate the canary and collect traces. if we still see OOMs we'll try increasing slab_size as a last resort (less ideal).

maria: logging note — when reproducing, use: `kubectl logs -l app=runtime -n canary --since=1h | grep "OOM workspace"` and gather `allocator.snap` files from hosts.

chen: posting PR link for sim in a few hours.

maria: awesome. will update thread with canary results.
